assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the old barbell club's post-meet athlete card press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single card, 127 x 178 mm (5 x 7 in) PORTRAIT, fonts embedded, produced from a real page-layout application so it converts cleanly to InDesign. Trim = media box, NO bleed box present (0 mm bleed).

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as five tidy blocks plus a crest and a photograph):
- Top: the LIFTER NAME in a bold condensed display face, large, in warm cream.
- A thin horizontal brass rule under the name.
- Middle: THREE STAT LINES stacked, each a label and a big number: SQUAT 000 / BENCH 000 / DEADLIFT 000.
- Below the stats: a QUOTE line, one line of italic text from the lifter.
- Top-right corner: the CLUB CREST, a small barbell-and-laurel roundel reading IRONSIDE BARBELL CLUB.
- Lower two-thirds: a large tinted PHOTO PANEL where the printed card shows the lifter's photograph.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The LIFTER NAME, the three STAT LINES and the QUOTE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame that flows top to bottom, with the stat numbers set as inline runs inside that flow; they are NOT five addressable frames and no individual stat line can be targeted on its own.
- The CLUB CREST is DRAWN vector artwork, a grouped set of paths, NOT a placed image.
- The tinted PHOTO PANEL is a DRAWN filled rectangle (a flat colour fill; on the original the print shop stripped the photograph in by hand at plate stage), NOT a rectangular picture/graphic frame; there is NO image well anywhere on the card, so a per-athlete portrait cannot be bound into it.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly: one flowing text frame + one grouped decorative path (the crest) + one filled rectangle (the panel) + one tiny footer story) is nothing like the five clean fields and the picture the printed card suggests, and there is NO graphic frame to carry a photograph.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not as visible tokens): LIFTER_NAME | SQUAT | BENCH | DEADLIFT | QUOTE

Colours: Forge Black #171310 ground, warm cream #EDE6D6 name and stats, Brass #A87B3A rule and crest, muted steel-olive #3A3C33 photo-panel tint.

assets.content:
ANVIL AND OAK - how the programming works and what the levels mean (from Mara and Deacon)

WHO RUNS IT
Two of us. Mara Voss and Deacon Hale. We ran a barbell club out of a shared space for six years before this and about half our people are coming with us. We coach, we don't sell memberships you don't use.

HOW THE PROGRAMMING WORKS
Everybody is on one system. You warm up the same movements every week - squat, press, pull, carry - and the load moves in a planned way, not by feel. New people run a simple linear progression until the easy jumps stop, then we move them onto four-week blocks that alternate volume and intensity. We write the program; you show up and do the work and add weight. That is the whole pitch. Show up, do the work, add weight. We handle the programming so you can focus on the bar.

WHAT THE LEVELS MEAN (this is the Level column on the roster)
- FOUNDATIONS: learning the lifts, empty bar to first real loads, coached closely. No meet pressure.
- STRENGTH: the main room. Running blocks, chasing lifetime numbers, training three to four days.
- COMPETITION: peaking for a platform, training around meets, attempts and openers planned with a coach.

A FEW LINES ON THE ROSTER
This is the opening group, the ones following us over plus a few new Foundations people. Rosa, Theo, Nadia and Sam have been with us the whole six years. Priya, Bex and Fiona are new this winter and moving fast. Dot came back to lifting at fifty and out-trains people half her age.

ONE THING ON CONSENT (important, do not miss this)
Reggie Tran asked us, after we pulled the roster export, to keep him OFF the cards and off the social posts for now. He is still training and still on the roster spreadsheet, we just never took him out of the export. Do NOT make a card for Reggie and do NOT put his portrait in the spotlight set. Everyone else is fine to feature. If the card count comes out one short of the roster, that is why.
